finding: The speed benchmark has only ever measured the BASH route. benchmarks/speed-benchmark.sh:86 hardcodes RUN_SH=autonomy/run.sh, so every number in this repo's speed corpus -- including the 392s agent line in gate-profile.json -- is from the route that does NOT apply prompt caching.
why_it_matters: The two routes differ on exactly the axis the agent line measures. loki-ts/src/runner/sdk_invoker.ts:54 sends the prompt as [static-prefix with cache_control:ephemeral, dynamic-tail], so the cache-stable prefix is billed once and reused. run.sh cannot: it pipes a single prompt string through `claude -p`, and the CLI exposes no way to express cache_control. run.sh:20139 says so honestly -- the [CACHE_BREAKPOINT] marker is 'a documentation anchor today'.
measured_prefix_size: 8090 bytes default, 1776 with LOKI_SIMPLE=1 (tests/test-simple-prompt-ablation.sh) -- roughly 1578 tokens of stable prefix re-sent every iteration on the bash route.
what_this_does_NOT_establish: That the Bun route is faster. Nobody has run it through this harness. Caching reduces input TOKEN COST and can reduce latency, but the agent's 392s is dominated by output generation and tool turns, and no measurement here separates those. Claiming a speedup from the mechanism alone would be exactly the reasoning this corpus refuses.
next_experiment: Teach speed-benchmark.sh to drive the Bun route, then run the same graded hard task on both with n>=6 per arm. That is the first comparison in this repo where a real mechanism predicts a direction in advance, which makes it worth the trials.
blocker: Not blocked. It needs a --route flag on the harness and a way to invoke loki-ts with the same caps; roughly an hour of harness work plus 3-4 hours of trials.

provenance_check_2026_08_09.why: Before spending hours on a two-route comparison, I checked that --route bun actually reaches the Bun path. It did not, twice, for two DIFFERENT reasons. Both would have produced a labelled-but-false corpus entry.
provenance_check_2026_08_09.bug_1_silent_bash_run: First smoke test recorded route=bash despite --route bun. Cause: the runner was selected with $( ... ) INSIDE the command line, which expands to a bare word rather than choosing a command -- the same class of error as the ${GRADER:+VAR=val} env-prefix bug fixed earlier the same day. Fixed by building the runner as an ARRAY before the subshell. The metrics label was also read from an env var set only inside the build subshell, so the parser never saw it; now passed explicitly.
provenance_check_2026_08_09.bug_2_bun_delegates_to_bash: Second smoke test recorded route=bun and STILL ran bash. Proof in the build log: the run.sh session banner appears TWICE and the bin/loki dispatcher line once. Cause is by design and documented at loki-ts/src/cli.ts:291-296 and bin/loki:300 -- `start` reaches the Bun RARV loop ONLY when LOKI_SDK_LOOP is 1 or true; otherwise the shim falls through to bash cmd_start. --route bun therefore measures bash unless LOKI_SDK_LOOP is also set.
provenance_check_2026_08_09.status: --route now labels honestly and the array fix is real, but the harness does NOT yet set LOKI_SDK_LOOP, so a bun-route comparison is still not runnable. That is a one-line change plus a re-verification that the build log shows no run.sh banner. NOT made here: benchmark work is paused by directive.
provenance_check_2026_08_09.evidence_preserved: The two smoke-test artifacts (speed-routesmoke*, speed-routesmoke2*) are the record; route=bash on the first and route=bun-but-bash-log on the second are the falsifying evidence, not noise.
